name: Gixo
summary: Seven separate AI workspaces — decks, articles, visuals, briefs, proposals, legal drafts and books — each sold on its own plan.
best_for: teams that want one dedicated, source-grounded tool per deliverable — a deck tool, a content tool, a proposal tool — and would rather buy them separately than bend one generic generator into every shape
skip_if: you want a single flat AI subscription covering writing and design together, or you cannot justify stacking three narrow products to cover what one all-in-one tool does under one price
honest_knock:
Two things about this pricing are worth reading twice.

The first is that seven products means seven subscriptions, and most of them are now per seat. Gixo is priced per deliverable, not per company, and one product's plan does not include the others. A team that needs decks, articles and proposals buys Lumen plus Quill plus Arc: $69 a month for one person at the entry tiers, $133 at the Starter tiers Gixo now recommends, and at least $759 a month for three people on the Professional tiers that add shared review. There is no published bundle price; the only route the page names is procurement, where private offers and multi-product bundles go through review. Ask for that before you subscribe to the second product, not after.

The second is the seat minimums (read 21 October 2026). On 4 October Quill Professional was $79 a month for three seats; it is now $79 a seat with a three-seat minimum, and every tier above the one-seat tiers on Quill, Lumen, Business, Lex and Arc works the same way. The generation allowance behind each tier is still not stated outside Folio's chapter counts, and the first step is steep on Quill: Lite at $10 is pitched at publishing now and then, the next tier is $59. Run the 14-day trial at the volume you actually expect.

pricing.notes: (re-read 2026-10-21 on gixo.ai/pricing in served HTML; the floors are unchanged, but the billing unit changed after our 4 October reading: five of the seven products are now priced per seat with a seat minimum per tier, where on 4 October each tier was one monthly price for a stated number of seats) Gixo is not one product but seven, each bought on its own plan, in USD. Per seat per month, with the annual figure per seat: Quill: Lite $10 (from 1 seat, $90 a year), Starter $59 (from 1 seat, $599), Professional $79 (minimum 3 seats, $799), Business $99 (minimum 5, $999), Enterprise $129 (minimum 10, $1,299). Lumen: Lite $10 ($90), Starter $25 ($250), Professional $45 (minimum 2, $450), Business $55 (minimum 5, $550), Enterprise $99 (minimum 10, $999). Business: Starter $19 ($190), Professional $49 (minimum 3, $499), Business $59 (minimum 5, $599), Enterprise $79 (minimum 10, $799). Lex: Solo Pilot $29 ($261), Solo $99 ($999), Small Firm $149 (minimum 3, $1,499), Growing Firm $179 (minimum 5, $1,799), Marketplace $229 (minimum 10, $2,299). Arc: Starter $49 ($490), Professional $129 (minimum 2, $1,299), Business $149 (minimum 5, $1,499), Enterprise $179 (minimum 10, $1,799). The FAQ says a team can add seats above each minimum. Prism and Folio still charge one price per plan for the seats it includes: Prism Starter $10 (1 seat, $90 a year), Professional $25 (2 seats, $250), Business $45 (5, $450), Enterprise $99 (10, $999); Folio Author $19 for 10 AI-drafted chapters a month and Pro $99 for 50, one seat each, with no annual figure. So the smallest bill on a tier with a seat minimum is the seat price times the minimum: Quill Professional at least $237 a month, Arc Professional $258, Lex Small Firm $447. Generation allowances are not quantified on the page except Folio's chapters. The FAQ still says a no-card 14-day trial with full generation, that continued generation after it needs a paid plan while existing work stays viewable, and that there is no standing unpaid tier. Folio is described three ways: “Monthly book plans” on its card, “14-day trial, no card” in the comparison table, and starting free for planning and import in the introduction. Quill, Lumen, Business, Arc and Lex can also be bought through Microsoft Azure Marketplace, where private offers and multi-product bundles are handled through procurement review.

schema_offer.description: Quill or Lumen Lite per seat, or Prism Starter per plan, per month, the lowest published entry tier (one seat) across seven separately sold products; since October 2026 Quill, Lumen, Business, Lex and Arc are priced per seat with a seat minimum per tier, so Quill Professional costs at least $237 a month (3 seats at $79); Prism and Folio charge one price per plan. Read on the vendor's own pricing page on 2026-10-21.

compare_with.name: Gamma or Beautiful.ai
compare_with.why: Gamma and Beautiful.ai do one job — turn a prompt into a presentable deck — and publish a single per-seat price you can multiply in your head. Gixo spreads the same AI drafting across seven separately priced products covering decks, content, visuals, briefs, proposals, legal work and books, so it reaches further and costs more to assemble. If decks are the whole job, the single-purpose tools are simpler and cheaper; if you want the same draft-review-export flow across several deliverables, that breadth is the thing Gixo actually sells. Verify all current price lists yourself; ours were read on 21 October 2026.

open_questions.question: Can a customer cancel at any time, and what happens to an annual plan that is cancelled mid-term?
Which data can a customer export, in which formats, on which plans?
Where is customer data stored, and can a customer choose the region?
Is there a minimum number of seats or users on any plan?

vendor_mcp.what: Remote server at gixo.ai/mcp. Six Lumen creation tools (pitch deck, board, sales and training presentations, from-URL, editable chart) and four analysis and routing tools work anonymously; execute_business_artifact needs a bearer token.
vendor_mcp.plan: Price not stated. Their docs split it by access instead: ten tools are anonymous and need no account, while business-artifact execution "requires a bearer token mapped to an entitled Gixo account".
vendor_mcp.note: The vendor's own MCP server, from our MCP research; it works with your own account at the vendor.
